title.zh: 卷三十四 志第四: 兵衞志上
title.raw: 卷三十四 志第四: 兵衞志上 Volume 34 Treatises 4: Military 1

sentences.zh: 兵衛誌上

translations.literal: Military Guards, Part 1
translations.idiomatic: Military Guards, Part 1

sentences.zh: 軒轅氏合符東海，邑於涿鹿之阿，遷徙往來無常處，以兵為營衛。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor combined tally-signs at the Eastern Sea, settled at the ford of Zhuolu, migrated without fixed abode, and used troops as camp and guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor united tally-signs at the Eastern Sea and settled at Zhuolu; the people moved without fixed homes and took the army as camp and guard.

sentences.zh: 飛狐以北，無慮以東，西暨流沙，四戰之地，聖人猶不免於兵衛，地勢然耳。

translations.literal: North of Feihu, east of Wulü, west to the drifting sands—a land of four-sided warfare; even a sage could not escape military guard; such was the terrain.
translations.idiomatic: From north of Feihu to east of Wulü and west to the drifting sands lay a land fought on every side; even a sage could not do without military guard—such was the terrain.

sentences.zh: 遼國左都遼海，右邑涿鹿，兵力莫強焉。

translations.literal: The Liao state held its left at Liaohai and its right at Zhuolu; nowhere was military strength stronger.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao state had Liaohai on the left and Zhuolu on the right; in military power none was stronger.

sentences.zh: 其在隋世，依紇臣水而居，分為十部。

translations.literal: In Sui times they dwelt along the Heichen River and were divided into ten divisions.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui they lived by the Heichen River and were split into ten divisions.

sentences.zh: 兵多者三千，少者千餘。

translations.literal: Where troops were many there were three thousand; where few, a little over a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The larger divisions mustered three thousand men, the smaller a little over a thousand.

sentences.zh: 順寒暑，逐水草畜牧。

translations.literal: They followed cold and heat, pursued water and grass, and pastured livestock.
translations.idiomatic: They followed the seasons, moved with water and pasture, and raised herds.

sentences.zh: 侵伐則十部相與議，興兵致役，合契而後動，獵則部得自行。

translations.literal: On raids the ten divisions deliberated together; to raise troops and impose service they united tally-signs before moving; on the hunt each division acted on its own.
translations.idiomatic: For invasion the ten divisions met in council; to raise armies and levy service they joined tally-signs before marching, but on the hunt each division went its own way.

sentences.zh: 至唐，大賀氏勝兵四萬三千人，分為八部。

translations.literal: By Tang times the Dahe clan had forty-three thousand able troops, divided into eight divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang the Dahe clan fielded forty-three thousand fighting men in eight divisions.

sentences.zh: 大賀氏中衰，僅存五部。

translations.literal: The Dahe clan declined; only five divisions remained.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dahe clan waned, only five divisions survived.

sentences.zh: 有耶律雅裏者，分五部為八，立二府以總之，析三耶律氏為七，二審密氏為五，凡二十部。

translations.literal: Yelü Yali divided the five into eight, established two offices to command them, split three Yelü clans into seven and two Shenmi clans into five—twenty divisions in all.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Yali split the five divisions into eight, set up two offices to oversee them, broke three Yelü lineages into seven and two Shenmi lineages into five—twenty divisions in all.

sentences.zh: 刻木為契，政令大行。

translations.literal: They carved wood for tally-contracts and government orders were widely enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Wooden tallies were carved for contracts, and government orders ran through the land.

sentences.zh: 遜不有國，乃立遙輦氏代大賀氏，兵力益振，即太祖六世祖也。

translations.literal: Xun did not hold the state; the Yaolian clan was raised to replace the Dahe, military strength grew ever stronger—this was the Taizu's sixth-generation ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun lost the realm the Yaolian clan replaced the Dahe and military power swelled—this was the Taizu's sixth-generation forebear.

sentences.zh: 及太祖會李克用於雲中，以兵三十萬，盛矣。

translations.literal: When the Taizu met Li Keyong at Yunzhong he had three hundred thousand troops—mighty indeed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu met Li Keyong at Yunzhong his host numbered three hundred thousand—a formidable army.

sentences.zh: 遙輦耶瀾可汗十年，歲在辛酉，太祖授鉞專征，破室韋、於厥、奚三國，俘獲廬帳，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yaonian Yelang Khan, the year xinyou, the Taizu received the battle-axe with sole command, broke the Shiwei, Yujue, and Xi states, and captured tents and households beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yaonian Yelang Khan, the year xinyou, the Taizu was given the battle-axe and sole command; he crushed the Shiwei, Yujue, and Xi and took tents and households past numbering.

sentences.zh: 十月，授大叠烈府夷離堇，明賞罰，繕甲兵，休息民庶，滋蕃群牧，務在戢兵。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was appointed yilijin of the Dayielie Office, made rewards and punishments clear, repaired armor and weapons, let the people rest, increased the herds, and strove to curb warfare.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he became yilijin of the Dayielie Office: rewards and punishments were made clear, arms were readied, the people were rested, herds were enlarged, and the aim was to still the armies.

sentences.zh: 十一年，總兵四十萬伐代北，克郡縣九，俘九萬五千口。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he commanded four hundred thousand troops to attack northern Dai, took nine commanderies and counties, and captured ninety-five thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he led four hundred thousand men against northern Dai, seized nine commanderies and counties, and took ninety-five thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 十二年，德祖討奚，俘七千戶。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Dezong attacked the Xi and captured seven thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Dezong campaigned against the Xi and took seven thousand households.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遙輦可汗卒，遺命遜位於太祖。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the Yaonian khan died and left orders that the throne pass to the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the Yaonian khan died and commanded that rule pass to the Taizu.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位五年，討西奚、東奚，悉平之，盡有奚、霫之眾。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of the Taizu's reign he attacked the western and eastern Xi, pacified them all, and wholly possessed the Xi and Mohe peoples.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of his reign the Taizu attacked western and eastern Xi, subdued them entirely, and held all the Xi and Mohe peoples.

sentences.zh: 六年春，親征幽州，東西旌旗相望，亙數百里。

translations.literal: In the sixth spring he personally campaigned against Youzhou; eastern and western banners faced one another for several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year he led a personal campaign on Youzhou; banners east and west stretched for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 所經郡縣，望風皆下，俘獲甚眾，振旅而還。

translations.literal: Every commandery and county he passed submitted at sight; captives were very many, and he returned in triumph.
translations.idiomatic: Commanderies and counties along the route surrendered at his approach; booty was immense, and he marched home in triumph.

sentences.zh: 秋，親征背陰國，俘獲數萬計。

translations.literal: In autumn he personally campaigned against the Beiyin state and captured tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he personally attacked the Beiyin state and took captives numbering in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 神冊元年，親征突厥、吐渾、党項、小蕃、沙陀諸部，俘戶一萬五千六百；

translations.literal: In the first year of Shence he personally campaigned against the Türks, Tuyuhun, Tangut, lesser tribes, and Shatuo—fifteen thousand six hundred households captured;
translations.idiomatic: In Shence year 1 he personally campaigned against the Türks, Tuyuhun, Tangut, lesser tribes, and Shatuo and took fifteen thousand six hundred households;

sentences.zh: 攻振武，乘勝而東，攻蔚、新、武、媯、儒五州，俘獲不可勝紀，斬不從命者萬四千七百級。

translations.literal: he attacked Zhenwu, pressed east on the momentum, attacked the five prefectures of Wei, Xin, Wu, Gui, and Ru, captured beyond counting, and beheaded fourteen thousand seven hundred who would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: he stormed Zhenwu, drove east on the momentum, overran Wei, Xin, Wu, Gui, and Ru, took booty past counting, and slew fourteen thousand seven hundred who refused submission.

sentences.zh: 盡有代北、河曲、陰山之眾，遂取山北八軍。

translations.literal: He wholly possessed the peoples of northern Dai, the river bend, and the Yin Mountains, and then took the eight armies north of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He held all the peoples of northern Dai, the river bend, and the Yin Mountains, then seized the eight armies north of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 四年，親征於骨裏國，俘獲一萬四千二百口。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he personally campaigned against the Yuguri state and captured fourteen thousand two hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he personally attacked the Yuguri state and took fourteen thousand two hundred captives.

sentences.zh: 五年，征党項，俘獲二千六百口。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he campaigned against the Tangut and captured two thousand six hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he campaigned against the Tangut and took two thousand six hundred captives.

sentences.zh: 攻天德軍，拔十有二柵，徙其民。

translations.literal: He attacked the Tiande Army, took twelve stockades, and moved the people away.
translations.idiomatic: He assailed the Tiande Army, carried twelve stockades, and relocated the inhabitants.

sentences.zh: 六年，出居庸關，分兵掠檀、順等州，安遠軍、三河、良鄉、望都、潞、滿城、遂城等縣，俘其民徙內地，皇太子略定州，俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he went out through Juyong Pass, divided troops to plunder Tan, Shun, and other prefectures, Anyuan Army, Sanhe, Liangxiang, Wangdu, Lu, Mancheng, Suicheng, and other counties, moved captives inland; the crown prince overran Dingzhou and took very many captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he issued through Juyong Pass, sent columns to raid Tan, Shun, and other prefectures and Anyuan Army, Sanhe, Liangxiang, Wangdu, Lu, Mancheng, Suicheng, and other counties, moved captives inland, while the crown prince overran Dingzhou with great booty.

sentences.zh: 天贊元年，以戶口滋繁，糺轄疏遠，分北大濃兀為二部，立兩節度以統之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianzan, because households had grown numerous and control was loose, northern Da Nongwu was split into two divisions and two military commissioners were set to command them.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianzan year 1, as households multiplied and oversight grew thin, northern Da Nongwu was divided in two and two commissioners were appointed to command them.

sentences.zh: 三年，西征党項等國，俘獲不可勝紀。

translations.literal: In the third year he campaigned west against the Tangut and other states; captives were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he marched west against the Tangut and other states and took captives past numbering.

sentences.zh: 四年，又親征渤海。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again personally campaigned against Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he again led a personal campaign against Bohai.

sentences.zh: 天顯元年，滅渤海國，地方五千里，兵數十萬，五京、十五府、六十二州，盡有其眾，契丹益大。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxian he destroyed the Bohai state—territory five thousand li, troops several hundred thousand, five capitals, fifteen prefectures, sixty-two prefectures—and wholly possessed their peoples; the Khitan grew greater still.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxian year 1 he destroyed Bohai—five thousand li of territory, armies in the hundreds of thousands, five capitals, fifteen prefectures, and sixty-two districts—and held all their people; Khitan power swelled further.

sentences.zh: 會同初，太宗滅唐立晉，晉獻燕、代十六州，民眾兵強，莫之能禦矣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huitong the Taizong destroyed Tang and established Jin; Jin offered the sixteen prefectures of Yan and Dai—the people numerous and troops strong, none could withstand them.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Huitong the Taizong ended Tang and raised Jin; Jin surrendered Yan and Dai's sixteen prefectures—populous lands and strong armies that none could resist.

sentences.zh: ○兵制

translations.literal: ○ Military System
translations.idiomatic: ○ Military System

sentences.zh: 遼國兵制，凡民年十五以上，五十以下，隸兵籍。

translations.literal: Liao military regulations: all commoners from fifteen up to fifty were entered on military registers.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liao military law every man from fifteen to fifty was registered for service.

sentences.zh: 每正軍一名，馬三匹，打草谷、守營鋪家丁各一人。

translations.literal: For each regular soldier one foraging-camp retainer and one camp-guard retainer; three horses per man.
translations.idiomatic: Each regular soldier had three horses plus one foraging-camp retainer and one camp-guard retainer.

sentences.zh: 人鐵甲九事，馬韉轡，馬甲皮鐵，視其力；

translations.literal: Nine iron armor pieces per man, horse saddle and bridle, horse armor of leather and iron according to strength;
translations.idiomatic: Each man bore nine pieces of iron armor; saddle, bridle, and horse armor of leather and iron were allotted by strength;

sentences.zh: 弓四，箭四百，長短槍、𨪷䤪、斧鉞、小旗、鎚錐、火刀石、馬盂、少一斗。

translations.literal: four bows, four hundred arrows, long and short spears, mattocks and hooked tools, axes and halberds, small flags, hammer-awls, fire-stone knives, horse cups—each short one peck.
translations.idiomatic: four bows, four hundred arrows, long and short spears, mattocks and hooked tools, axes and halberds, small flags, hammer-awls, fire-stone knives, and horse cups—each man one peck short in grain.

sentences.zh: 少袋、搭钅毛傘各一，縻馬繩二百尺，皆自備。

translations.literal: One small pouch and one felt umbrella each, two hundred feet of tether rope—all self-provided.
translations.idiomatic: Each also carried one small pouch and one felt umbrella and two hundred feet of tether rope, all at his own cost.

sentences.zh: 人馬不給糧草，日遣打草谷騎四出抄掠以供之。

translations.literal: Men and horses were not issued grain or fodder; daily they sent foraging cavalry in four directions to raid and supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Neither men nor horses received rations; each day foraging cavalry rode out in four directions to plunder for supplies.

sentences.zh: 鑄金魚符，調發軍馬。

translations.literal: Gold fish tallies were cast to mobilize armies and horses.
translations.idiomatic: They cast gold fish tallies to dispatch armies and horses.

sentences.zh: 其捉馬及傳令有銀牌二百。

translations.literal: Those who seized horses and bore orders had two hundred silver plaques.
translations.idiomatic: Horse-catchers and order-bearers held two hundred silver plaques.

sentences.zh: 軍所舍，有遠探欄子馬，以夜聽人馬之聲。

translations.literal: Where the army encamped there were distant-scout barricade horse scouts to listen at night for the sound of men and horses.
translations.idiomatic: At every camp distant-scout barricade horse scouts listened through the night for the sound of men and horses.

sentences.zh: 凡舉兵，帝率蕃漢文武臣僚，以青牛白馬祭告天地、日神，惟不拜月，分命近臣告太祖以下諸陵及木葉山神，乃詔諸道征兵。

translations.literal: Whenever troops were raised the emperor led Khitan and Han civil and military officials, sacrificed with blue ox and white horse to Heaven and Earth and the sun god—only not bowing to the moon—and separately ordered close ministers to announce to the tombs from the Taizu down and to the god of Mount Muye, then decreed levies from every circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When armies were raised the emperor led Khitan and Han officials, offered blue ox and white horse to Heaven, Earth, and the sun—never the moon—and sent close ministers to report to the tombs from the Taizu onward and to Mount Muye's god before decreeing levies on every circuit.

sentences.zh: 惟南、北、奚王，東京渤海兵馬，燕京統軍兵馬，雖奉詔，末敢發兵，必以聞。

translations.literal: Only the southern king, northern king, Xi king, Eastern Capital Bohai troops, and Yanjing commander-in-chief's troops—though they received the decree—dared not march until they had reported.
translations.idiomatic: Even the southern king, northern king, Xi king, Eastern Capital Bohai forces, and Yanjing commander's troops, though they received the decree, would not march until they had reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上遣大將持金魚符，合，然後行。

translations.literal: The court dispatched a great general bearing the gold fish tally; only when tallies matched did they move.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent a great general with the gold fish tally; only when the tallies joined did the columns march.

sentences.zh: 始聞詔，攢戶丁，推戶力，核籍齊眾以待。

translations.literal: At first word of the decree they gathered household men, weighed household strength, checked registers, and mustered the host to wait.
translations.idiomatic: On first hearing the decree they mustered household men, weighed each household's capacity, reconciled registers, and assembled the host to wait.

sentences.zh: 自十將以上，次第點集軍馬、器仗。

translations.literal: From commanders of ten upward they mustered troops and gear in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: From leaders of ten men upward they mustered troops and weapons in due order.

sentences.zh: 符至，兵馬本司自領，使者不得與。

translations.literal: When the tally arrived the original bureau led the troops itself; envoys might not take command.
translations.idiomatic: When the tally arrived the home bureau itself led the troops; the envoy might not take them over.

sentences.zh: 唯再共點軍馬訖，又以上聞。

translations.literal: Only after jointly counting the troops again did they report upward.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a second joint muster of troops and gear did they report upward.

sentences.zh: 量兵馬多少，再命使充軍主，與本司互相監督。

translations.literal: According to the size of the force they again appointed an envoy as army commander to supervise jointly with the home bureau.
translations.idiomatic: They gauged the host's size and again named an envoy as army commander to supervise jointly with the home bureau.

sentences.zh: 又請引五方旗鼓，然後皇帝親點將校。

translations.literal: They also requested the five-direction banners and drums; then the emperor personally inspected officers.
translations.idiomatic: They also called for the five-direction banners and drums; only then did the emperor personally review the officers.

sentences.zh: 又選勛戚大臣，充行營兵馬都統、副都統、都監各一人。

translations.literal: Meritorious kin and great ministers were again chosen as camp army commander, deputy commander, and overseer, one each.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious kin and great ministers were chosen as camp army commander, deputy commander, and overseer, one of each.

sentences.zh: 又選諸軍兵馬尤精銳者三萬人為護駕軍，又選驍勇三千人為先鋒軍，又選剽悍百人之上為遠探欄子軍，以上各有將領。

translations.literal: From every army the finest thirty thousand were chosen as the imperial guard corps; three thousand bold men as vanguard; groups of a hundred or more of the fiercest as distant-scout barricade horse corps—each with its own officers.
translations.idiomatic: From all armies thirty thousand elite troops formed the imperial guard; three thousand daring men the vanguard; bands of a hundred or more of the boldest the distant-scout barricade horse corps—each with its officers.

sentences.zh: 又於諸軍每部。

translations.literal: Again in each army unit.
translations.idiomatic: Again, within each army unit:

sentences.zh: 量眾寡，抽十人或五人，合為一隊，別立將領，以備勾取兵馬，騰遞公事。

translations.literal: According to numbers, five or ten men were drawn from each unit, formed into a squad with its own leader, to requisition troops and relay official business.
translations.idiomatic: By strength, five or ten men were taken from each unit, formed into a squad under its own leader, to levy troops and carry urgent dispatches.

sentences.zh: 其南伐點兵，多在幽州北千里鴛鴦泊。

translations.literal: For southern campaigns troops were mustered mostly a thousand li north of Youzhou at Mandarin-Duck Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Southern campaigns were mustered chiefly at Mandarin-Duck Marsh, a thousand li north of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 及行，並取居庸關、曹王峪、白馬口、古北口、安達馬口、松亭關、榆關等路。

translations.literal: On the march they took the routes of Juyong Pass, Caowang Vale, White Horse Ford, Gubei Pass, Anda Horse Ford, Songting Pass, Yuguan, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: On the march they used Juyong Pass, Caowang Vale, White Horse Ford, Gubei Pass, Anda Horse Ford, Songting Pass, Yuguan, and the like.

sentences.zh: 將至平州、幽州境，又遣使分道催發，不得久駐，恐踐禾稼。

translations.literal: As they neared Pingzhou and Youzhou territory envoys were again sent on separate roads to hurry them on—they might not linger long, lest they trample the grain.
translations.idiomatic: Near Pingzhou and Youzhou they sent envoys on separate roads to hurry the columns—they could not linger, lest they tread the crops.

sentences.zh: 出兵不過九月，還師不過十二月。

translations.literal: Troops might not issue after the ninth month; return might not pass the twelfth month.
translations.idiomatic: Armies might not march out after the ninth month nor return after the twelfth.

sentences.zh: 在路不得見僧尼、喪服之人。

translations.literal: On the road they might not meet monks, nuns, or persons in mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: On the march they might not encounter monks, nuns, or mourners in funeral dress.

sentences.zh: 皇帝親征，留親王一人在幽州，權知軍國大事。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned in person one close prince was left at Youzhou to act for military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor led the campaign himself one imperial prince remained at Youzhou with authority over army and state.

sentences.zh: 既入南界，分為三路，廣信軍、雄州、霸州各一。

translations.literal: Once within the southern border they divided into three routes—Guangxin Army, Xiongzhou, and Bazhou each one.
translations.idiomatic: South of the border they split into three columns—Guangxin Army, Xiongzhou, and Bazhou each had one.

sentences.zh: 駕必由中道，兵馬都統、護駕等軍皆從。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage must take the middle road; the army commander and guard corps all followed.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage always took the center; the army commander and guard corps followed it.

sentences.zh: 各路軍馬遇縣鎮，即時攻擊。

translations.literal: Troops on each route attacked county seats and towns as soon as they met them.
translations.idiomatic: Each column attacked every county seat and market town it met.

sentences.zh: 若大州軍，必先料其虛實、可攻次第而後進兵。

translations.literal: Against great prefectural armies they first gauged strength and feasible order of attack before advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Before a great prefectural army they first judged its strength and the sequence in which it could be taken.

sentences.zh: 沿途民居，園囿、桑柘，必夷伐焚蕩。

translations.literal: Along the way they leveled and burned gardens, orchards, and mulberry and catalpa groves.
translations.idiomatic: Along the route they cut down and burned gardens, orchards, and mulberry and catalpa plantings.

sentences.zh: 至宋北京，三路兵皆會，以議攻取。

translations.literal: At the Song Northern Capital all three armies met to deliberate the assault.
translations.idiomatic: At the Song Northern Capital the three hosts united to plan the assault.

sentences.zh: 及退亦然。

translations.literal: On retreat it was the same.
translations.idiomatic: On the withdrawal it was the same.

sentences.zh: 三路軍馬前後左右有先鋒。

translations.literal: Before, behind, left, and right of the three armies were vanguards.
translations.idiomatic: Vanguards rode before, behind, left, and right of the three armies.

sentences.zh: 遠探欄子馬各十數人，在先鋒前後二十餘里，全副衣甲，夜中每行十里或五里少駐，下馬側聽無有人馬之聲。

translations.literal: Distant-scout barricade horse scouts, a dozen or so each, lay twenty-odd li before and behind the vanguard, in full armor; at night they marched ten or five li and halted briefly, dismounted and listened sideways for the sound of men and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Barricade horse scouts in bands of a dozen lay twenty-odd li ahead and behind the vanguard in full armor; at night they rode ten or five li, halted briefly, dismounted, and listened for men or horses.

sentences.zh: 有則擒之；

translations.literal: If there were any, they seized them.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone detected was seized.

sentences.zh: 力不可敵，飛報先鋒，齊力攻擊。

translations.literal: If strength could not match the enemy, they flew word to the vanguard and attacked together.
translations.idiomatic: If they could not overcome the foe they raced word to the vanguard and struck together.

sentences.zh: 如有大軍，走報主帥。

translations.literal: If there was a great army they ran to report the commander.
translations.idiomatic: If a great host appeared they galloped to warn the commander.

sentences.zh: 敵中虛實，動必知之。

translations.literal: The enemy's true strength and movements were always known.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy's real strength and every movement were always known.

sentences.zh: 軍行當道州城，防守堅固，不可攻擊，引兵過之。

translations.literal: When the army passed a prefectural city on the main road that was stoutly defended and could not be taken, they led the troops past it.
translations.idiomatic: If a prefectural city on the main road was too strong to storm, they led the host past it.

sentences.zh: 恐敵人出城邀阻，乃圍射鼓噪，詐為攻擊。

translations.literal: Fearing the enemy would sally to intercept, they surrounded it, shot arrows, and shouted as if attacking.
translations.idiomatic: Lest the garrison sally to block them, they ringed the walls, shot, and shouted as though attacking.

sentences.zh: 敵方閉城固守，前路無阻，引兵進，分兵抄截，使隨處州城隔絕不通，孤立無援。

translations.literal: The enemy shut the gates and held firm; the road ahead was clear, the army advanced, and detachments cut communications so every prefectural city stood isolated without aid.
translations.idiomatic: The foe barred the gates; the road ahead lay open; the host pressed on while detachments severed links so every city stood alone without relief.

sentences.zh: 所過大小州城，至夜，恐城中出兵突擊，及與鄰州計會軍馬，甲夜，每城以騎兵百人去城門左右百餘步，被甲執兵，立馬以待。

translations.literal: At every large or small prefectural city by night—fearing troops would sally or neighboring prefectures would combine forces—at the first watch a hundred horsemen went a hundred-odd paces from each gate in armor with weapons, standing by their mounts.
translations.idiomatic: At night, at every city great or small, lest the garrison sally or neighboring forces unite, at the first watch a hundred horsemen in armor with weapons waited a hundred paces from each gate beside their mounts.

sentences.zh: 兵出，力不能加，馳還勾集眾兵與戰。

translations.literal: If troops came out and strength could not prevail, they galloped back to gather the host and fight.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy sallied and they could not prevail, they raced back to muster the host and give battle.

sentences.zh: 左右官道、斜徑、山路、河津，夜中並遣兵巡守。

translations.literal: Official highways, bypaths, mountain roads, and river crossings were all patrolled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Main roads, side paths, mountain tracks, and river fords were patrolled through the night.

sentences.zh: 其打草谷家丁，各衣甲持兵，旋團為隊，必先砍伐園林，然後驅掠老幼，運土木填壕塹，攻城之際，必使先登，矢石檑木並下，止傷老幼。

translations.literal: Foraging-camp retainers each wore armor and bore arms, wheeling into squads; they first cut orchards, then drove off the old and young, hauled earth and timber to fill moats and ditches, and at assault must climb first—stones, bolts, and beams fell only on the old and young.
translations.idiomatic: Foraging-camp retainers wore armor, formed rotating squads, felled orchards first, then drove off the aged and children and hauled earth and timber to fill ditches; at the assault they climbed first while missiles fell mainly on the old and young.

sentences.zh: 又於本國州縣起漢人鄉兵萬人，隨軍專伐園林，填道路。

translations.literal: From home prefectures and counties ten thousand Han militia were also raised to march with the army, dedicated to felling gardens and filling roads.
translations.idiomatic: From the realm's prefectures and counties ten thousand Han militia marched with the host to fell gardens and fill roads.

sentences.zh: 禦寨及諸營壘，唯用桑柘梨栗。

translations.literal: Imperial camps and all stockades used only mulberry, catalpa, pear, and chestnut.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial camps and every stockade used only mulberry, catalpa, pear, and chestnut.

sentences.zh: 軍退，縱火焚之。

translations.literal: On withdrawal they set fire and burned them.
translations.idiomatic: On withdrawal they burned them all.

sentences.zh: 敵軍既陣，料其陣勢小大，山川形勢，往回道路，救援捷徑，漕運所出，各有以制之。

translations.literal: Once the enemy had formed battle lines they gauged the formation's size, the mountains and rivers, roads in and out, rescue shortcuts, and where supplies came from—each had its counter.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy formed ranks they measured the array, terrain, roads, relief paths, and supply lines—each had its countermeasure.

sentences.zh: 然後於陣四面，列騎為隊，每隊五、七百人，十隊為一道，十道當一面。

translations.literal: Then on four sides of the formation cavalry were ranged in squads of five to seven hundred; ten squads made a file, ten files a front.
translations.idiomatic: Then on all four sides of the enemy line cavalry stood in squads of five to seven hundred; ten squads a file, ten files a front.

sentences.zh: 各有主帥。

translations.literal: Each had its commander.
translations.idiomatic: Each front had its commander.

sentences.zh: 最先一隊走馬大噪，沖突敵陣。

translations.literal: The foremost squad galloped with great shouting and charged the enemy line.
translations.idiomatic: The leading squad galloped shouting and smashed into the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 得利，則諸隊齊進；

translations.literal: If they prevailed, all squads advanced together.
translations.idiomatic: On success every squad charged together.

sentences.zh: 若未利，引退，第二隊繼之。

translations.literal: If they did not prevail they withdrew; the second squad followed.
translations.idiomatic: If they failed they drew off and the second squad took their place.

sentences.zh: 退者，息馬飲水料。

translations.literal: Those who withdrew rested horses, drank water, and fed fodder.
translations.idiomatic: The withdrawn men rested their horses, watered them, and fed grain.

sentences.zh: 諸道皆然。

translations.literal: Every file did the same.
translations.idiomatic: Every file did likewise.

sentences.zh: 更退叠進，敵陣不動，亦不力戰。

translations.literal: They advanced again in rotation; if the enemy line did not move they did not press hard either.
translations.idiomatic: They rotated forward in waves; if the enemy line held firm they did not press the fight.

sentences.zh: 歷二三日，待其困憊，又令打草谷家丁馬施雙帚，因風疾馳，揚塵敵陣，更互往來。

translations.literal: After two or three days, when the foe was weary, foraging-camp retainers were ordered to fit double brooms on their horses and ride with the wind, raising dust across the enemy line back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: After two or three days, when the foe was spent, foraging retainers fixed double brooms to their horses and rode with the wind, whipping dust across the enemy ranks back and forth.

sentences.zh: 中既饑疲，目不相睹，可以取勝。

translations.literal: Midst hunger and exhaustion they could not see one another and victory could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Hungry and worn, the enemy could scarcely see one another—and victory could be won.

sentences.zh: 若陣南獲勝，陣北失利，主將在中，無以知之，則以本國四方山川為號，聲以相聞，得相救應。

translations.literal: If the southern wing won and the northern wing lost, the commander in the center could not know; they used the realm's mountains and rivers as signals, calling by name to rescue one another.
translations.idiomatic: If the southern wing won while the northern wing lost, the commander at the center might not know; they called by the names of the homeland's mountains and rivers to signal and rescue one another.

sentences.zh: 若帝不親征，重臣統兵不下十五萬眾，三路往還，北京會兵，進以九月，退以十二月，行事次第皆如之。

translations.literal: If the emperor did not campaign in person, a great minister commanding no fewer than a hundred fifty thousand followed the three routes there and back, mustering at the Northern Capital—out in the ninth month, back in the twelfth—the sequence of actions was the same.
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor stayed home, a great minister led no fewer than a hundred fifty thousand on the three routes, mustering at the Northern Capital—out in the ninth month, back in the twelfth—with the same sequence of actions.

sentences.zh: 若春以正月，秋以九月，不命都統，止遣騎兵六萬，不許深入，不攻城池，不伐林木，但於界外三百里內，耗蕩生聚，不令種養而已。

translations.literal: If in spring from the first month or in autumn from the ninth month no commander-in-chief was appointed, only sixty thousand cavalry were sent—they might not penetrate deep, storm cities, or cut timber, but only within three hundred li of the border wear down settlements and forbid planting and raising stock.
translations.idiomatic: In spring from the first month or autumn from the ninth month, if no commander-in-chief was named, only sixty thousand horsemen went—they might not penetrate deep, take walled cities, or fell trees, but within three hundred li of the border they harried settlements and forbade planting and husbandry.

sentences.zh: 軍入南界，步騎軍帳不循阡陌。

translations.literal: Once the army entered the southern border, infantry and cavalry camps did not follow field paths.
translations.idiomatic: South of the border infantry and cavalry camps did not keep to field paths.

sentences.zh: 三道將領各一人，率欄子馬各萬騎，支散遊弈百十里外，更叠覘邏。

translations.literal: Each of the three routes had one commander leading ten thousand barricade horse scouts each, dispersed in roaming patrols a hundred or ten li out, relieving one another in watch.
translations.idiomatic: Each route had one commander with ten thousand barricade horse scouts, scattered in roaming patrols a hundred or ten li out, relieving one another in observation.

sentences.zh: 及暮，以吹角為號，眾即頓舍，環繞禦帳，自近及遠，折木稍屈，為弓子鋪，不設槍營塹柵之備。

translations.literal: At dusk the horn was the signal and all halted; they ringed the imperial camp from near to far, bending branches into bow-shaped shelters—no stockades, spear lines, moats, or palisades.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk a horn sounded and all encamped, ringing the imperial tent from near to far with bent branches for bow-shaped shelters—no stockades, spear lines, moats, or palisades.

sentences.zh: 每軍行，鼓三伐，不問晝夜，大眾齊發。

translations.literal: Whenever the army marched, three drum beats—day or night—sent the whole host forward together.
translations.idiomatic: On every march three drum rolls—day or night—sent the whole host forward at once.

sentences.zh: 未遇大敵，不乘戰馬，俟近敵師，乘新羈馬，蹄有餘力。

translations.literal: Before meeting a great enemy they did not ride war horses; only near the enemy did they mount fresh horses with strength to spare.
translations.idiomatic: Before a great battle they did not ride their war horses; only near the foe did they mount fresh horses still full of vigor.

sentences.zh: 成列不戰，退則乘之。

translations.literal: In formation they did not fight; on retreat they rode.
translations.idiomatic: In the line they held back; on retreat they charged.

sentences.zh: 多伏兵斷糧道，冒夜舉火，上風曳柴。

translations.literal: They set many ambushes to cut grain routes, lit fires by night, and dragged brush upwind.
translations.idiomatic: They laid many ambushes to sever supply lines, lit fires by night, and dragged brush upwind.

sentences.zh: 饋餉自賫，散而復聚。

translations.literal: Provisions they carried themselves, scattering and gathering again.
translations.idiomatic: They carried their own provisions, scattering and regathering.

sentences.zh: 善戰，能寒。

translations.literal: Skilled in battle, able to endure cold.
translations.idiomatic: They fought well and bore the cold.

sentences.zh: 此兵之所以強也。

translations.literal: This is why their troops were strong.
translations.idiomatic: This is why their armies were strong.
